tutor.title: An AI tutor
tutor.question: Why does my loop print 0, 1, 2 and not 1, 2, 3?
tutor.answer: range(3) starts counting at 0, so you get three numbers ending at 2. range can also take a number to start from: which one would give you 1, 2, 3?
tutor.followUpAnswer: Close. range stops just before its second number, so range(1, 3) gives 1 and 2. What would the stop need to be for 3 to make it in?
tutor.picture: A student asks why their loop prints 0, 1, 2 instead of 1, 2, 3. The tutor explains that range starts at 0, and when the student tries range(1, 3), that range stops just before its second number, leaving the last step to them.

rules.radioPrivacyDesc: The optional Focus Radio plays one royalty-free instrumental track we host ourselves: no third parties, no cookies, no ads. It's a single live broadcast, so everyone tuned in hears the same moment. Nothing loads until you press play. Prefer silence? Just leave it paused.
rules.tutorPrivacyDesc: When you chat with the tutor, your messages and the conversation so far, plus the page you're on, are sent to a third-party AI provider (Google Gemini) to write the answer. In a chat about a lesson or challenge, the statement, your code, the end of your last run and your last test result go with them. Don't paste personal or sensitive information into the chat or the editor. Your newest 50 conversations are saved, each with its newest 200 messages, until you delete them. The tutor works in 5-hour sessions worth between 15 and 30 messages. It's an optional aid: you can complete every lesson without it.
